excerpt: Ramp combines corporate cards, expenses, bill pay and accounting automation for US businesses. Its free and paid plans, funding to a $44 billion valuation, and alternatives.
content:
Ramp is a finance platform for businesses. It started with corporate cards and has grown to cover expense management, travel booking, bill payments, procurement, accounting automation and business banking, with AI tools that collect receipts, code transactions and flag spending outside policy.

Ramp was founded in 2019 by Eric Glyman, its chief executive, and Karim Atiyeh, its chief technology officer. The two had earlier built Paribus, a consumer savings app that Capital One bought in 2016.

Its valuation has climbed quickly. In November 2025 it raised $300 million at a $32 billion valuation, and in June 2026 it announced a $750 million round led by ICONIQ, GIC and Ontario Teachers' Pension Plan at a $44 billion valuation, saying it had passed $1 billion in annualised revenue, according to FinTech Futures. In October 2026 Bloomberg reported that Ramp had raised about $1.85 billion more at roughly a $60 billion pre-money valuation, led by Dragoneer and Thrive Capital; Ramp declined to comment and had not announced it.

Ramp has been built for US companies. With its June 2026 round it said it planned to bring its corporate card and spend tools to UK and European companies.

There are three plans. Ramp Free costs nothing per user; Ramp Plus adds more automation and controls for $15 per user a month, with a 30-day free trial; and Enterprise is custom-priced.

We have not used Ramp for this page. It brings together Ramp's own website and pricing page and reporting from the outlets linked under Sources, and says where each fact comes from.

use_cases: Issuing corporate cards with per-card limits and controls
Automatic receipt matching and expense reports
Paying vendor bills by ACH, card, check or wire
Syncing coded transactions to QuickBooks Online or Xero
Booking business travel within a company policy

fit: US startups and companies that want cards, expenses and bill pay in one system
finance teams that want to cut manual receipt chasing and coding
companies on QuickBooks or Xero looking for automated bookkeeping
not_fit: companies outside the US: check Ramp's eligibility first, since its UK and European launch was only announced in 2026
sole traders who just need a personal-style card

pricing.intro: Ramp's pricing page lists three plans. Prices are per user per month in US dollars.

plans.name: Free
plans.detail: Unlimited cards, expenses via SMS or Slack, travel booking, bill pay, invoices, basic accounting rules, QuickBooks Online and Xero integrations

plans.name: Plus
plans.detail: More automation and controls; 30-day free trial; procurement available as an add-on

plans.name: Enterprise
plans.detail: Workday and Oracle Fusion integrations, local-currency cards in 30+ countries, dedicated support and implementation services

notes: Ramp says Plus can be paid by ACH or with rewards earned on the Ramp card.

items.name: Brex
items.difference: Ramp's closest rival, with a strong push into global companies.

items.name: Navan
items.difference: Started from corporate travel and added expenses.

items.name: Expensify
items.difference: Long-standing expense tool with its own card.

items.name: Bill.com (BILL)
items.difference: Focused on bills and invoices rather than cards.

pros: Cards, expenses, bills and accounting in one product
Heavy use of automation to reduce manual finance work
cons: Advanced controls and integrations need Plus or Enterprise

faq.a: Yes. Ramp Free costs $0 per user. Ramp Plus is $15 per user a month and Enterprise is custom-priced, per Ramp's pricing page on 15 October 2026.
Eric Glyman (CEO) and Karim Atiyeh (CTO) founded Ramp in 2019.
Ramp announced a $44 billion valuation in June 2026. Bloomberg reported in October 2026 a new raise at about $60 billion pre-money, which Ramp had not confirmed.
Ramp has been built for US companies; check its eligibility rules. Its Enterprise plan lists local-currency card issuing in 30+ countries for global companies.
